prerequisites: Successfully passed exams in Electrical Engineering
Successfully passed exams in Fundamentals of Structural Mechanics
Ability to perform Taylor series expansions
Ability to perform Fourier series expansions

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the operating modes and specifications of instrumentation for measurements and controls on mechanical and thermal systems.
Be able to choose, manage, and use measurement instrumentation rationally.
Evaluate measurement uncertainty and its main causes in applications.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of the concept of measurement
Application of measurement instrumentation in various fields, particularly in controls
Concept of measurement and uncertainty
Configuration of a measurement instrument
Functional block diagram
Characteristics of measurement chains and signal analysis
Static calibration and static characteristics of an instrument: uncertainty, sensitivity, linearity, repeatability, threshold, resolution, hysteresis, dead space, scale readability, input impedance
Uncertainty in indirect measurements
Dynamic characteristics, generalized mathematical model of a measurement system
Zero-order, first-order, and second-order instruments
Response to canonical inputs
Response of a general instrument model to a periodic input
Response of a general instrument model to a transient input
Elements of analog and digital signal analysis: spectra, correlations, transfer functions
Main electrical and electronic components of measurement chains for data manipulation, transmission, acquisition, processing, and presentation
Classic systems for mechanical and thermal measurements
Classic systems for measuring lengths, displacements, deformations, velocities of solids (translation and rotation), accelerations, forces, pressure, acoustic noise, heat fluxes, temperature
Study of samples, static and dynamic calibration methods, and usable instruments for each physical quantity
Description of the operating principle of all instruments
Critical evaluation of instrument performance and fields of application
Criteria for instrument selection
Methods for interpreting experimental data obtained from instruments
Laboratory exercises involving calibration and/or use of displacement transducers
Laboratory exercises involving calibration and/or use of strain gauges
Laboratory exercises involving calibration and/or use of accelerometers
Laboratory exercises involving calibration and/or use of pressure sensors
Laboratory exercises involving calibration and/or use of microphones
Laboratory exercises involving calibration and/or use of load cells
Laboratory exercises involving calibration and/or use of thermocouples
Laboratory exercises involving calibration and/or use of thermoresistors
Laboratory exercises involving calibration and/or use of oscilloscopes
Laboratory exercises involving calibration and/or use of spectrum analyzers
Laboratory exercises involving calibration and/or use of data acquisition systems on personal computers
assessment_rules: The exam consists of an oral exam and/or a written exam. The oral exam, lasting approximately 45 minutes, assesses the student's knowledge and comprehension of theoretical and methodological content, as well as communication skills. The written exam, lasting no more than 60 minutes, consists of multiple-choice tests to verify the ability to correctly apply theoretical knowledge, understand proposed problems, and communicate in writing.
